reference_plate.objective: Read a finite section of |ζ(σ+it)| and locate the critical line among neighboring samples.
reference_plate.equation: Euler–Maclaurin expansion with N=96 through B6
reference_plate.domain: 27 real parts from 0 to 1, 169 imaginary parts from 8 to 32

minimum-scale.objective: Compare the guaranteed positive contribution in a primal direction with the exact zero in the chosen test direction for the dual estimate.
minimum-scale.numerical_method: Exact integer enumeration of points a²+b²<4d in Gaussian coordinates, with a²+b²≤d for full weight. The sum of full-weight squared lengths supplies a numerator bound and the number of candidates bounds Z. The displayed fractional lower bound is reduced exactly.

kernel-order.objective: Evaluate the same paired kernel in the two integration orders, identify the conjugated input, and bound the omitted terms before cancellation.
kernel-order.numerical_method: Exact Gaussian-integer partial sums with powers of two as denominators. A parity sum over the two source coordinates is compared with the pairing on the two-point target. The infinite absolute tail is bounded by the complement of the finite square in a convergent product of positive series.

central-period.objective: Compare the period on a full unit cycle with the integral on a movable open arc, including open arcs where cancellation gives equality at particular basepoints.
central-period.numerical_method: The sine difference in the antiderivative is evaluated exactly at eighth-turn endpoints and the result is also rounded to four places when irrational. The solid coefficient curve is drawn through 97 samples.

rank-grid.objective: See how the nine independently chosen entries of a four-by-four array determine every value when all coordinate sums vanish.
rank-grid.numerical_method: Exact products of signed indicator differences at two coordinates of one free orbit for T=5. The two selectors move the basis vector through all nine positions.

euler.objective: See the residue-degree substitution and the effect of two split primes versus one inert prime in the same unramified quotient.
euler.numerical_method: Real powers in binary64, finite products evaluated algebraically. Four base residue sizes and 0.5 ≤ s ≤ 4. A rank-(1,8) algebraic illustration with trivial parameters.

marks.objective: Use the location of the exceptional twists to select one entire multiplicative window.
marks.numerical_method: Selection in base-two logarithmic coordinates with exact dyadic endpoints. The 289 ordered input pairs at exponents 0 through 16 are compared with their forbidden intervals.

floor-sum.objective: Compare the signed floor sum with the special value and examine the unit hypothesis.
floor-sum.numerical_method: Exact integer arithmetic for all units modulo 5, 25 or 125, multipliers 2, 3 and 4, trivial primitive character and k = 2.

jacobi-primes.objective: Lift a cubic character at a chosen split prime, then test the same Jacobi sum and its partner at both primes above p.
jacobi-primes.numerical_method: Count products in {1,ω,ω²} at p = 7, 13 and 19 using the defining power congruence. Reduce in the integral basis (1,ω), multiply the conjugates and evaluate at both roots. All computations are exact. Independent tests enumerate powers of a primitive generator for all six settings.

split-endpoint.objective: Count intermediate lattices above a fixed rank-two endpoint and see how the split Euler factor removes their multiplicity.
split-endpoint.numerical_method: At residue size 2, 3, 4 or 5, compare the coefficient recurrence with Hermite counts for every excess length through 6. Apply the quadratic correction by convolution. The largest uncorrected coefficient is 19531.

gram-pair.objective: Distinguish the diagonal isometry error from overlap between words and see which errors survive an isometric column restriction.
gram-pair.numerical_method: Two normalized two-column maps in real four-space. Compute squared Hilbert–Schmidt sums for both words and their cross block on the full spaces and on the selected coordinate lines. All 18 settings are independently tested by taking inner products of the original scaled columns.

prism.objective: Recover the weight power and the scalar gluing index from the actual alternating prism.
prism.numerical_method: Enumerate all 5ᵉ cyclic words and every insertion in F₁₁× at twist one or two. Products of integer carries and logarithmic indices are reduced modulo five.

satake-average.objective: See how twelve right-K cosets with three induced weights determine the zonal value on one entire double class. Reciprocal parameters can give different weights and the same mean.
satake-average.numerical_method: For the selected exact rational α, calculate nine copies of α/3, two of 1 and one of 3/α. Sum in rational arithmetic and divide by twelve. Floating point is used only for chart coordinates. The six-setting test independently filters the rank-two matrix representatives by their minimum entry valuation.

inert-length.objective: Read a lattice length from the two surviving rows of 3G and see how cancellation changes it even with all entry valuations fixed.
inert-length.numerical_method: For s ∈ {1,2} and t ∈ {0,1,2}, reduce the entries in 𝔽₃[i]/(i²+1). Subtract s times row 3 from row 1, count the pivots, and take nine to that power to find the quotient size. The independent test enumerates every residue-field row combination of the scaled matrix.

inert-cell.objective: Follow the two independent residue sizes through the row count, the corner count, and the number of cosets of one exact length.
inert-cell.numerical_method: With middle rank one and standard middle lattice, evaluate the exact ball counts, then difference successive cumulative counts. The smallest shell starts at length |a|.

flag-average.objective: Compare the distribution of signed line averages for three point configurations and recover the incidence norm on the mean-zero subspace.
flag-average.numerical_method: Enumerate every normalized homogeneous line over the four displayed finite fields. Count by signed sum and use integer arithmetic for both squared norms. The approximate ratio is rounded to four significant digits.

mobius-product.objective: Separate cancellation over the full divisor set from the coefficient that remains after the two length restrictions.

shear-rounding.objective: Read the Schur-complement coordinate correction as a choice of lattice point in a Gaussian basis.
shear-rounding.numerical_method: Round coordinates in fifths, compute both exact quadratic-form distances in units of 1/25 and display their physical positions in the complex plane.

fourier-rank.objective: Observe the loss from retaining only full-rank Fourier frequencies in a finite model of the comparison.
fourier-rank.numerical_method: Enumerate the three independent matrix entries and count all trace phases modulo 3 for each of the 27 frequencies. Character orthogonality reduces their averages exactly.

height-grid.objective: Distinguish the number of grid candidates for one height label from the separate multiplicity of rational classes per centre.
height-grid.numerical_method: Exact counts of integer numerators at all four ordered depths in a two-coordinate, one-real-place grid with R=1. Compare their product to the independent uniform power bound.

trace-cycles.objective: Distinguish one trace around a cycle from a product of traces, and read off how place and block repetition affect a contraction.
trace-cycles.numerical_method: Explicit sums of diagonal matrix entries for the identity and of transposed pairs of entries for the swap, across all selected blocks and supports.

hermitian-density.objective: Relate an unramified Whittaker factor to an explicit count of Hermitian frames at an inert place, and see how congruence lifting preserves the normalized density.
hermitian-density.numerical_method: Enumerate all unit vectors and their ordered orthogonal pairs over the nine-element residue field. At each higher level use the smooth fibre multiplicity 3^(2mn−n²). Compare the result to the Euler polynomial at the special point.

orbit-weights.objective: Distinguish matrix labels and distinct orbit points when normalizing a compactly supported arithmetic partition.
orbit-weights.numerical_method: Two Gram matrices of rank two over ℤ[ω] have 72 preimages each. Direct enumeration of short integer columns checks both multiplicities. Divide each raw weight by the sum over all labels.
